Off-by-one errors, explained by cats. An off-by-one error is a loop that runs one time too few or too many. In Python, range stops before its end number, so range(1, 3) only gives 1 and 2.

#offbyone #python #learntocode #CATding #programming #coding #catmemes

Git, explained by cats. Git saves snapshots of your work. Commit to save, log to see history, checkout to bring an old version back, branch to experiment safely and merge to keep the result.

#git #learntocode #github #CATding #programming #coding #catmemes

The wedding invite scam, explained by cats. A wedding invitation on WhatsApp that ends in .apk is an app, not an invitation. Installed, it can read your SMS bank codes and empty your account. Real invites are photos, PDFs or links.

#scam #cybersecurity #indonesia #CATding #tech #learnontiktok #catmemes

Password hashing, explained by cats. Good websites never store your password. They store a hash: a one-way scramble that can't be reversed. Plus salt and a slow hash like bcrypt. If a site can email you your password, run.

#cybersecurity #passwords #python #CATding #tech #learnontiktok #catmemes

ChatGPT, explained by cats. ChatGPT writes by guessing the next piece of text, over and over, based on patterns from huge amounts of text. Usually right, sometimes confidently wrong, so check anything important.

#chatgpt #ai #artificialintelligence #CATding #tech #learnontiktok #catmemes

Noise cancelling, explained by cats. Noise-cancelling headphones listen to the noise around you and play the exact opposite wave, so peaks meet valleys and cancel out. Great for a steady hum, weak against a sudden bark.
